gaps: How is 'harness-owned' determined, given init/adopt use repo_root() as their source — which the vendored gate tests set to the CLIENT repo, so there is no separate harness reference to iterate?
The vendored factory-scaffold workflow runs the harness's own regression suite in every client; some tests bind to symphony-forge's private FORGE-INIT-1 fixtures and can never pass elsewhere.
resolutions: Resolved: a HARDCODED harness-owned manifest (whitelist), defined once and shared by init, adopt and upgrade. Because the source is repo_root() (the client under the vendored tests), the commands cannot distinguish harness-owned by iterating a separate tree — they must copy exactly the known harness paths (.claude/{CLAUDE.md, settings.json, skills/forge}, .codex config + harness agents + skills/forge) and nothing else from the source's .claude/.codex. This subsumes the reported skills-canon bug and also keeps a client's custom .codex content out of a scaffold. A test asserts init/adopt/upgrade agree on the set.

Resolved by human decision (this session): GATE the fixture-bound tests — they skip when their symphony-forge fixture (.factory/history/FORGE-INIT-1) is absent, so the vendored workflow passes in a client while still running every portable check and still running the fixture tests in symphony-forge's own CI. (The alternative, dropping pytest from the vendored workflow, was rejected: clients keep running the harness regression suite.)
summary: The capability is well-scoped: init and adopt must vendor only harness-owned .claude/.codex machinery (a shared whitelist manifest), and the vendored regression suite must skip symphony-forge-only fixture tests in a client. Root cause confirmed against the code — all three commands source from repo_root(), so only a hardcoded manifest is safe. The two substantive choices (manifest whitelist; gate vs drop the harness tests) were put to the human and resolved. No contradiction with active decisions (0014 specs-before-build satisfied; 0016 machinery-dir ownership). Ready to confirm.
